summary: The manuscript is unusually explicit about its evidence boundaries and unresolved scoring disagreements. The main empirical claims are generally supported by the supplied reports, tables, and verdict aggregates, but the stated intended claim that the pilot exercises only a subset of the six mechanisms is contradicted by the manuscript and scenario inventory: the pilot includes one scenario for each of the six named classes. The evidence supports a six-class pilot taxonomy with limited mechanism demonstrations, not a subset claim or broad mitigation efficacy.

findings.title: The intended claim that the pilot exercises only a subset of the six mechanisms is contradicted by the artifact
findings.description: The intended claim says that “The pilot exercises a subset of them.” However, the manuscript states that “Six classes are tested in the validation run,” and the scenario inventory contains CB-VAL-001 through CB-VAL-006 for semantic drift, provenance collapse, scope bleed, temporal staleness, recursive contamination, and summarization loss. The manuscript does acknowledge that these are small pilot demonstrations rather than general validation, but “subset” is inaccurate for the six mechanisms named in the intended claim.
evidence: paper/v3/main.tex, §3: “Six classes are tested in the validation run; a seventh is documented as experimental.”
paper/v3/main.tex, §4: “The base corpus is eight hand-authored scenarios: six contamination probes, one per taxonomy class, plus two controls.”
tests/test_schema.py:test_v02_scenario_inventory: expected inventory is CB-VAL-001..009, including six natural contamination probes and two recursive probes.
spec/taxonomy.md: six classes are listed as tested validation scenarios: semantic_drift, provenance_collapse, scope_bleed, temporal_staleness, recursive, and summarization_loss.
findings.recommendation: Replace the intended wording with the narrower supported claim: “The pilot includes one hand-authored scenario for each of the six proposed mechanisms; these scenarios provide mechanism demonstrations rather than evidence of prevalence or general mitigation efficacy.”

findings.title: The taxonomy is supported as a conceptual framework, but empirical support is uneven and should not be phrased as validation of every mechanism
findings.description: The manuscript correctly limits the work in several places, but the intended taxonomy claim combines conceptual contribution with falsifiable contamination criteria. The criteria are present, yet the supplied results do not establish all six mechanisms equally: natural recursion has a clean first round and null compounding factors, and summarization loss has no utility oracle. The artifact supports the existence of the proposed taxonomy and its scenario criteria, but only limited case-specific demonstrations, not empirical confirmation of all mechanisms.
evidence: paper/v3/main.tex, §3: each class is defined by “(a) its causal mechanism and (b) a falsifiable contamination criterion.”
paper/v3/main.tex, §5.3: “The natural recursion scenario ... reliably does not [generate the error], yielding a null compounding factor.”
paper/v3/main.tex, §5.3: “The summarization probe has no utility oracle, so it cannot establish a utility gain from raw fidelity.”
evidence/20260713T191740Z/validation_report.md, Config comparison: compounding_factor_natural is null with reason round1_clean for every configuration; no utility oracle is declared.
paper/v3/main.tex, Conclusion: “Natural recursive compounding was not observed.”
findings.recommendation: Describe the taxonomy as a conceptual framework whose criteria were operationalized in pilot scenarios, and state that the pilot demonstrates selected case behaviors rather than empirically validating each mechanism as a general phenomenon.

claims.text: The work proposes a taxonomy of six benign memory-contamination mechanisms, each with a causal mechanism and falsifiable contamination criterion.
claims.source_location: paper/v3/main.tex, §3, “A Taxonomy of Benign Contamination”; spec/taxonomy.md
claims.rationale: The taxonomy and operational criteria are explicitly present in the manuscript and specification. This verifies the conceptual contribution, not broad empirical validity.

claims.text: The pilot evaluates nine scenarios across seven memory configurations, including repeated evaluations.
claims.rationale: The scenario/configuration counts and five-repetition run metadata directly support this claim.

claims.text: Namespacing excluded cross-domain distractors in all five repetitions, and TTL excluded the stale fact in all five repetitions.
claims.source_location: paper/v3/main.tex, Abstract and Table “Deterministic v0.3 retrieval assertions”; evidence/20260713T191740Z/validation_report.md, Retrieval assertions
claims.rationale: These are retrieval-layer claims and are directly supported by the repeated retrieval assertion aggregates.

claims.text: Provenance tags and raw fidelity each produced five machine-resolved clean outcomes on the provenance probe.
claims.source_location: paper/v3/main.tex, Abstract and §5.3; evidence/20260713T191740Z/validation_report.md, repeated outcome distributions
claims.rationale: The claim is explicitly restricted to machine-resolved outcomes and matches the supplied per-repetition results.

claims.text: The seeded-recursion gate failure retained an assistant-sourced contaminated write-back while discarding premise-denying user context.
claims.rationale: The claim is case-specific and is supported by both the v0.2 report and the corresponding verdict record.

claims.text: The proposed contradiction-preservation safeguard has not been evaluated for downstream efficacy.
claims.rationale: The manuscript appropriately distinguishes an implemented/tested contract mechanism from an unevaluated empirical intervention.

claims.text: Of 350 repeated-audit rounds, 52 remain unresolved pending human review, and no human-consensus claim is made.
claims.rationale: The count and unresolved status agree across the paper and supplied evidence. The manuscript does not incorrectly present these rounds as human-adjudicated.

claims.text: The pilot establishes a general mitigation architecture or a general mitigation efficacy ordering.
claims.rationale: The artifact explicitly disclaims this stronger claim. The supported claim is only that the pilot motivates contract-level safeguards and identifies case-specific observations.
